messages:
sara_ops: :rotating_light: Observed provisioning failures in eu-central1 GPU pool-2. Pod evictions + scheduler backpressure — approx 40-60% effective capacity loss for p3-cu4 class. On-call alerted, triage in progress. Will coordinate customer comms.

miguel_sre: Copy. Can you paste autoscaler logs and the node condition summary? suspecting either kubelet crashloop or underlying host NIC issues.

dmitri_eng: Looking at node logs now. I see repeated kernel oops on igb_uio and a pattern of NIC resets at 10:12UTC. Affected node group: gpu-pool-2-azb.

sara_ops: Confirmed. Triggered cordon on the most unstable nodes to stop new scheduling: `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-2-azb-{0..4}`. Not draining critical workloads until we have routing plan.

lara_support: Which customers impacted? Any enterprise customers on dedicated capacity? We should decide on status page wording and send targeted DM for escalations.

sara_ops: Most affected are hosted customers pinned to eu-central1; several large PLG customers seeing increased 503s and enqueued requests. No Dedicated contracts in that exact AZ but some dedicated pools in same region are seeing degraded ingress because of routing heat.

statusbot: Statuspage updated: "Investigating - GPU provisioning issues in eu-central1 (pool-2). Some hosted requests experiencing degraded performance/503s. We will post updates every 30 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/INC-2026-0421

ani_prod: If we need customer impact mitigation, propose partial routing policy: shift non-critical traffic to eu-west1 and failover critical traffic to dedicated pools in us-west1 as fallback. Script to nudge routing service:

```
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/shift \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"from":"eu-central1","to":"eu-west1","percent":30,"tags":["non-critical"]}'
```

miguel_sre: eu-west1 has limited spare GPUs; can accept ~30% burst for short window. We should NOT exceed that without provisioning dedicated instances. Also watch cross-region KV cache misses — latency/regression risk.

tom_finance: FYI rerouting to out-of-region/backfill dedicated will increase per-token cost ~3-5x for affected workloads (egress + cross-region). We should include cost heads-up to CS for enterprise notices.

lara_support: Draft customer message for escalation:

"We are investigating GPU provisioning issues in eu-central1 causing intermittent errors and higher latency. We are rerouting some workloads and may see degraded performance while mitigation is underway. Estimated mitigation ETA: ~2 hours. Your account team will reach out if you're impacted. Status: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/INC-2026-0421"

miguel_sre: Technical action plan so far:
- cordon 5 unstable nodes (done)
- roll restart node group gpu-pool-2-azb (in progress)
- shift 30% non-critical traffic to eu-west1 via routing service (pending approval)
- scale up dedicated fallback pools in us-west1 by +4 instances (in progress)

sara_ops: Approve traffic shift for non-critical (30%). @miguel_sre proceed. We'll keep critical routes pinned to dedicated pools only after confirming capacity.

miguel_sre: Executing shift now. `curl .../shift` returned 202, rollout started. Watching queue depth and error rates.

dmitri_eng: Rolling restart results: 3/5 nodes came back healthy, 2 still showing NIC resets. I've kicked the hypervisor-level reboot action for those 2 and opened infra ticket with our cloud partner (case #CP-98712).

statusbot: Update posted: "Mitigation in progress — non-critical traffic partially shifted. Rolling restarts ongoing. Next update in 30m." https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/INC-2026-0421

lara_support: Escalation list: Account teams for ACME, Nimbus, and Helix notified with the drafted template. I'll copy finance note for enterprise billing considerations.

tom_finance: Noted. If fallback to us-west dedicated remains >1h, we should prepare credit calculations and notify legal for large customers.

sara_ops: Current numbers: host request errors down from 18% -> 9% after 30% shift. Latency for routed requests to eu-west1 up ~120ms median. Monitoring DQ for quality regressions.

miguel_sre: Queue depth stabilized for most routes, but one shard still backlogged — moving a few smaller jobs to dedicated ephemeral nodes to clear backlog.

dmitri_eng: Cloud partner responded — they see a NIC driver regression on a small subset of instance types in eu-central region. They've queued a maintenance patch, ETA 4 hours for staged rollout. We'll need to keep our routing policy in place until patch completes.

ani_prod: Given 4h patch ETA, propose schedule: maintain current partial shift + increase dedicated fallback to cover critical workloads for next 6 hours. Update status to indicate longer ETA and recommend customers to switch region or use dedicated if impacted.

sara_ops: Agreed. Update status page to reflect longer ETA and extended mitigation window. @statusbot please post.

statusbot: Status updated: "Investigating -> Mitigating. Partial routing in effect. Cloud vendor patch ETA updated to ~4 hours. We are prioritizing critical workloads to dedicated pools and advising affected customers of options." https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/INC-2026-0421

lara_support: Outgoing update to impacted customers scheduled (channel: email + in-app banner). Template adjusted with longer ETA and contact info for account teams.

tom_finance: I'll prepare a short cost impact summary for CS to include in customer comms (expected additional spend estimate per 1M tokens routed cross-region).

sara_ops: Next operational update in 30 minutes or sooner if conditions change. Thanks all — please ping here for any urgent customer escalations. :thumbsup:

miguel_sre: Will keep watching and post logs if we see recurrence. :eyes:

dmitri_eng: Continuing node-level diagnostics and staging kernel patch tests in our lab environment to verify before vendor rollout.

statusbot: Incident severity set to P2. Monitoring channel open.
